newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - McDonald's says Arch Deluxe successful.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - McDonald's says Arch Deluxe successful.

text.p: McDonald's Corp, which on Thursday introduced a new fish and two new chicken sandwiches to its U.S. menu, said its four-month-old Arch Deluxe sandwich continues to beat its expectations.
"We think it's been enormously successful," Vice Chairman Jack Greenberg said in a telephone interview. "We sold over 100 million (Arch Deluxe) sandwiches in the first month."
Greenberg said the May introduction of the Arch Deluxe hamburger was 38 percent better than expectations.
"And it's still doing over projection," he added.
He countered criticism about the sales performance of the Arch Deluxe, saying McDonald's did not expect the sandwich to turn around the competitive U.S. market all by itself.
Some analysts, pointing to a decline in McDonald's U.S. same store sales, have said the Arch Deluxe was not successful.

"The sales environment is very tough in the United States," Greenberg said. "We don't believe that any single product can make an enormous difference like it might have 20 years ago when all you were selling was hamburgers and cheeseburgers..."
Greenberg declined to comment specifically on U.S. same store sales, which many analysts expect will show a decline in the third quarter following a soft July and August.
"The sales environment continues to be tough and very competitive, and I don't see any change in that from prior quarters," Greenberg said.

Despite the U.S. market, McDonald's, which continues to expand rapidly overseas, is expected to report a rise in third quarter earnings. First Call shows a mean of analysts' earnings projections of $0.64 a share, up from $0.56 last year.

However, the addition of the new Crispy Chicken Deluxe, Grilled Chicken Deluxe and Fish Filet Deluxe sandwiches in the United States should help increase the size of the average customer check and raise the profit on menu items. "The penny profit on these new sandwiches is better," Greenberg said.

Dean Witter analyst David Adelman said the deluxe sandwiches on McDonald's menu will help McDonald's meet consumers' demands for more variety and more flavorful sandwiches. "I think rolling out these sandwiches is the right strategy," he added.

While some McDonald's customers have been substituting, or "trading off", the Arch Deluxe for other menu items they normally purchase, Greenberg said the new burger continues to add incrementally to sales.
"We see it adding incremental sales, yes. That doesn't change the fact that this is continuing to be a very difficult sales environment in the U.S...," Greenberg said.
Competition in the United States is compounded by the growth in the number of quick-service restaurants which is outpacing increases in "eating away from home" occasions.
